baseline.name: Telemanom (Hundman et al., KDD 2018)
baseline.source_detail: Table 2, Non-Parametric w/ Pruning (p = 0.13); also khundman/telemanom README

notes: Protocol: every row of telemanom's labeled_anomalies.csv is one stream (55 SMAP rows / 69 anomalies, 27 MSL rows / 36 anomalies). P-2 (SMAP) is listed twice with slightly different labels; like telemanom we score both rows, using one model. T-10 has data files but no label row, so it is not evaluated.
Event-level scoring per the paper: a labeled sequence overlapped by any predicted sequence is a TP; unmatched labeled sequences are FN; predicted sequences overlapping no label are FP.

Hyperparameters are the paper's defaults (l_s=250, 2x80 LSTM, dropout 0.3, batch 64, <=35 epochs, early stopping patience 10 / min_delta 3e-4; thresholding batch 70, window 30, smoothing 5%, buffer 100, p=0.13). Nothing was tuned on the test labels.

Differences from telemanom: PyTorch instead of Keras; best-validation weights restored after early stopping; no C-2 special case (telemanom hard-codes one for that channel); the last thresholding window judges all its new points.
Baseline F1 is derived from the paper's reported precision/recall; the paper reports F0.5.
Point-adjusted F1 is point-wise with segment-level adjustment. It is optimistic and not comparable to the event-level numbers.
